title: Weckle is a molecular switch that diverts Toll signalling from innate immunity towards growth by engaging Yki
authors: Perez-Sanchez MD; Li G; Moncrieffe M; Rojo-Cortés F; Malinovska K; Sample E; Maddick M; Moreira M; Connolly E; Parsons A; Feuda R; Gay NJ; Hidalgo A
one_liner_zh: 该文研究转录因子Wek在Toll信号通路中与Yki互作调控生长，虽涉及转录因子但未聚焦DNA结合机制，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: The mechanisms underlying how the brain can switch from a plastic to a degenerative state are unknown. Tolls and Toll-Like receptors (TLRs) could be involved since they underlie both neuroinflammation and structural brain plasticity. Here, we show that the Toll signalling adaptor Weckle (Wek) - a ZAD-Zinc-finger transcription factor - can switch the response from promoting innate immunity or cell death, to inducing growth instead. Myristoylated Wek binds Tolls at the membrane, and concerted PI3K and Toll signalling drive its nuclear translocation. Wek interacts with Yorkie (Yki) – the key regulator of growth restrained by Hippo - enabling its nuclear shuttling. Remarkably, Wek blocks innate immunity. Instead, Wek and Yki together drive glial cell proliferation and growth. Through this mechanism, Toll signalling could promote structural brain plasticity via Wek and Yki downstream. As Tolls and Yki are widespread, these findings could have important implications for understanding also regeneration and cancer.
abstract_zh: 大脑从可塑性状态转变为退行性状态的潜在机制尚不清楚。Tolls和Toll样受体（TLRs）可能参与其中，因为它们既介导神经炎症，也介导结构性大脑可塑性。在此，我们表明Toll信号适配器Weckle（Wek）——一种ZAD-锌指转录因子——能够将响应从促进先天免疫或细胞死亡切换为诱导生长。肉豆蔻酰化的Wek在膜上结合Tolls，而协同的PI3K和Toll信号驱动其核转位。Wek与Yorkie（Yki）——受Hippo抑制的生长关键调控因子——相互作用，使其能够进行核穿梭。值得注意的是，Wek阻断先天免疫。相反，Wek和Yki共同驱动胶质细胞增殖和生长。通过这一机制，Toll信号可能通过下游的Wek和Yki促进结构性大脑可塑性。由于Tolls和Yki广泛分布，这些发现也可能对理解再生和癌症具有重要意义。
